chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Muawiya, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Khallad ibn as-Saffar, who said:
Abu Abdillah was asked: Is al-Qa'im born? He said: No. If I were to live to see him, I would serve him during the days of my life.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.أَيَّامَ حَيَاتِي: the days of my life, indicating the duration of the Imam's life
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: al-Qa'im (The Riser/Imam), a title for the Awaited Imam

ai.seo_question: Was al-Qa'im born at the time of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the Awaited Imam (al-Qa'im) is confirmed as not yet born, establishing the timeline of the occultation within Twelver Shia eschatology. The Imam’s declaration of personal readiness to serve him highlights the continuity of spiritual authority and the intimate connection between the Imams and the Mahdi, reinforcing the concept of the 'Hidden Imam' who is alive but concealed. This hadith is frequently cited in discussions regarding the duration of the Major Occultation and the legitimacy of the Imam's lineage.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (46) Ali bin Ahmad al-Bandaneeji narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi from al-Hasan bin Mo’awiya from al-Hasan bin Mahboob that Khallad bin as-Saffar had said:
“Once Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) was asked: Is al-Qa’im born?” He said: “No, he is not. If I live until he is born, I shall serve him as long as I live.”
